title: Titan clients load no _Wrath TOCs and match no game type, so publishers' Titan builds are refused
description:
## Background

The `titan` client-rules row in `src/rules.rs` (Wrath Titan-Reforged, China, 3.80.x, interface 38002) lists no game types and no game suffixes. Both were marked UNVERIFIED, and `tests/toc_matrix.rs` asserted the empty row. So a Titan client loads only a plain `Folder.toc` or a `_Classic` family TOC, and every `AllowLoadGameType` directive excludes it.

The catalog probe (omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.7) found three addons whose publishers declare Titan but which omaddons refuses there: WeakAuras, Questie and Plater. Evidence from the live archives, 2026-10-15:
- WeakAuras 5.22.1 declares `titan:38002`. Its only TOC for Titan is `WeakAuras_Wrath.toc` with `## Interface: 38002`, which is Titan's interface (Wrath Classic is 30405), and `## AllowLoadGameType: wrath, titan`. So the Titan client loads `_Wrath` TOCs, and its game type is `titan`.
- Questie declares `wrath:38002` for the same reason.
- Plater v661 declares `titan:38001` but ships no TOC with a 38xxx interface. That is a publisher mismatch, not this bug.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build a synthetic Battle.net tree with `wow_classic_titan` (3.80.2).
2. `omaddons install weakauras -t titan --dry-run --json`.
3. Result: `no_compatible_release`, with every WeakAuras folder `no_loadable_toc`, although release.json declares titan.

## Technical Approach

- `titan` row: `game_types = ["titan"]`, `game_suffixes = ["Wrath"]`; the family suffix stays `Classic`.
- Record the evidence (and its date) in the row's doc comment in place of the UNVERIFIED note. `_Titan` stays out; nothing shows a client reads it.
- Update the TOC matrix comment and add curated rows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `_Wrath.toc` with Interface 38002 is the loaded, compatible TOC on titan.
- `AllowLoadGameType: wrath, titan` loads on titan; `AllowLoadGameType: wrath` alone does not.
- `install weakauras -t titan` installs on a synthetic Titan client, as release.json declares.
- The catalog probe's titan column agrees with every publisher except listed publisher mismatches.
- `argc gate` passes, with the builtin rules-table snapshot updated.

## Test Plan

- TOC matrix rows on titan: a `_Wrath` TOC with 38002 is compatible; `_Wrath` with 30405 is `interface_not_in_family`; game type `titan` is allowed; `AllowLoadGameType: wrath` is excluded.
- The suffix sweep follows the row automatically.
- Live: `catalog_matches_declared_flavors` titan column.

## Considerations

- Titan is a China-only client and not on the development machine; this rests on publisher archives, which ship what Titan players actually use.
- If a publisher later ships `_Titan.toc`, add the suffix with that evidence.
acceptance_criteria: _Wrath.toc with Interface 38002 loads and is compatible on titan; AllowLoadGameType wrath, titan loads on titan and wrath alone does not; weakauras installs on a synthetic titan client; the catalog probe titan column agrees except listed publisher mismatches; argc gate passes with the rules snapshot updated
close_reason: The titan rules row now has game type titan and game suffix Wrath, from publishers' archives: WeakAuras 5.22.1 ships WeakAuras_Wrath.toc with Interface 38002 (Titan's alone) and AllowLoadGameType wrath, titan; Questie declares wrath:38002. The UNVERIFIED notes in src/rules.rs and tests/toc_matrix.rs are replaced by that evidence.

comments.author: RustyDolphin
comments.text: claim: src/rules.rs titan row, tests/toc_matrix.rs, tests/fixtures/toc/matrix/cases.toml

comments.author: RustyDolphin
comments.text: done: argc gate passes; TOC matrix rows on titan (_Wrath 38002 loaded and compatible over _Vanilla; _Wrath 30405 interface_not_in_family; AllowLoadGameType wrath alone game_type_excluded; Wrath Classic rejects the 38002 _Wrath TOC); the suffix sweep follows the row; tests/install_multi_flavor.rs installs a WeakAuras-shaped release (with its _Wrath TOC) on a synthetic titan client; builtin rules snapshot updated; live catalog probe titan column now agrees for WeakAuras and Questie (Plater's titan:38001 is a listed publisher mismatch: no 38xxx TOC). decided: no _Titan suffix until a publisher ships one · found: none

title: Epic: Classic and Forever real-client gaps found after M1
description:
## Background

The M1 checkpoint (omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.7.10) closed on 2026-10-15 with real-machine evidence for two clients only: retail and the 3.3.5a AzerothCore client. WoW: Forever was proven only against a synthetic target, and no live Classic client existed on the development machine.

Later the same day the owner installed every live Classic client and the Forever stress-test client on the development machine, booting each Classic client once so its `Interface/AddOns` exists. The Battle.net root (`<home>/Games/battlenet/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft/`) now holds:

| Folder | Product | Version | Interface | Family | Game modes it runs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `_retail_` | `wow` | 12.1.5.70391 | 120105 | mainline | Retail |
| `_classic_era_` | `wow_classic_era` | 1.15.9.70003 | 11509 | vanilla | Classic Era, Hardcore, Season of Discovery |
| `_classic_` | `wow_classic` | 5.5.4.70268 | 50504 | mists | Mists of Pandaria Classic |
| `_anniversary_` | `wow_anniversary` | 2.5.6.70006 | 20506 | tbc | Burning Crusade Anniversary |
| `_forever_` | `wowf` | 1.60.1.70245 | 16001 | forever | Forever stress test (never launched: no `Interface/`, no `WTF/`) |

Discovery found all six clients correctly (`omaddons status --json`). Checking them turned up the gaps this epic closes:

1. **Bug:** DBM and BigWigs are refused on every non-retail client, although both publishers declare Classic Era, Anniversary, Mists Classic and Forever builds. The verifier refuses an archive when any one folder is for another client, and both ship retail-only boss-module folders beside their shared core.
2. **Bug:** installing into a client that has never been launched (no `Interface/AddOns`) fails with a `plan_stale` error that claims to be retryable and fails identically on every retry. `--dry-run` reports success. The real Forever client is in this state until the 2026-10-19 stress test.
3. **Gap:** Season of Discovery and Hardcore have no target name. They run in the Classic Era client (`era`), `-t sod` and `-t hardcore` are `target_not_found`, and nothing in the output says where they went.
4. **Gap:** no real-machine test covers the three Classic clients.
5. **Gap:** no real-machine test covers the real Forever client, and no one has confirmed that the client actually loads what omaddons installs.
6. **Gap:** nothing compares omaddons' verdicts against the flavors each publisher declares in `release.json`. That is how bug 1 shipped: the checkpoint recorded BigWigs v427.6 and DBM 12.1.14 as "no Forever build yet" on Forever, but both releases declare `forever:16001`.

## Goals

- Every catalog addon installs on every client its publisher declares, skipping only the folders that client would not load, and is refused everywhere else.
- A first install into a never-launched client works, and `--dry-run` predicts the real run.
- Players can name a client by the game mode they play (`sod`, `hardcore`), and `status` says which modes share a client.
- Real-machine smoke tests cover all six clients on the development machine.
- A live probe keeps omaddons' verdicts in step with publishers' declared flavors, so a regression like bug 1 fails a checkpoint instead of hiding in an expected-looking refusal.
- The installed addons are confirmed to load in the real Forever client during the 2026-10-19 stress test.

## Success Criteria

- Every child bead is closed.
- `argc gate` passes; contract snapshots are updated for the additive JSON fields.
- `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE=1 OMADDONS_LIVE=1 cargo test --test real_machine -- --ignored --test-threads=1` passes on the development machine and leaves every AddOns folder as it found it.
- `OMADDONS_LIVE=1 cargo test --test live_probes -- --ignored` passes, including the catalog × flavor probe.
- `omaddons install dbm bigwigs -t era|anniversary|classic|forever` installs on the development machine.

## Non-Goals

- M2 work: `update`/`outdated`, WoWInterface/Tukui, dependencies, adopt, sync, search.
- Separate addon sets per game mode. The game shares one `Interface/AddOns` between Classic Era, Hardcore and SoD; omaddons cannot split it.
- CurseForge or Wago builds of DBM/BigWigs.
- Titan, Cata or Wrath Classic real clients (none installed); they are covered by synthetic targets in the live probe only.

## Considerations

- Dates: the Forever stress test opens 2026-10-19; Forever launches 2026-11-04 (omad-wez re-checks publishers after launch).
- Publishers republish often; fixture tests pin layouts copied from the 2026-10-15 releases, and live probes check the current ones.
- Blizzard moves game modes between clients (Anniversary realms ran in the Classic Era client before `_anniversary_` existed), so the mode table is data, not code (vision D15).
- Contract changes here are additive (new fields); the contract freezes only at the first tag (M4).
acceptance_criteria: Every child bead is closed; argc gate passes with contract snapshots updated; OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE=1 OMADDONS_LIVE=1 real_machine suite passes on the development machine and leaves every AddOns folder as found; OMADDONS_LIVE=1 live_probes suite passes including the catalog x flavor probe; omaddons install dbm bigwigs succeeds on era, anniversary, classic and forever on the development machine

title: Multi-flavor archives with retail-only modules are refused on every non-retail client (DBM, BigWigs)
description:
## Background

DBM and BigWigs ship one zip for every client. Each zip holds shared folders whose TOC lists every client's interface, plus retail-only boss-module folders gated to retail. Both publishers' `release.json` declare the zip for Classic Era, Anniversary, Mists Classic, Titan, Cata, Wrath and Forever as well as retail. The game loads the shared folders and ignores the retail-only ones.

omaddons refuses the whole archive on every non-retail client. `compatible()` in `src/engine/inspect.rs` accepts an archive only when some folder is `Compatible` **and no folder is `WrongFlavor`**. `try_candidate()` in `src/engine/plan.rs` then rejects the candidate with `wrong_flavor: ...`, and the item fails `no_compatible_release`. The boss-mod entries of the catalog are therefore unusable on every Classic client and on Forever.

Layouts verified on 2026-10-15 (top-level folders and their TOC headers):

**DBM** (`gh:DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods`, `DBM-Core-12.1.14.zip`; release.json flavors `mainline:120100/120105, classic:11509, bcc:20506, wrath:30405, titan:38002, cata:40402, mists:50504, forever:16001`):

| Folder | `## Interface` | `## AllowLoadGameType` |
|---|---|---|
| DBM-Core | 11509, 16001, 20506, 30405, 38002, 40402, 50504, 120100, 120105 | none |
| DBM-GUI | same list | none |
| DBM-StatusBarTimers | same list | none |
| DBM-VPVEM | same list | none |
| DBM-Brawlers | 120100, 120105 | standard |
| DBM-Midnight | 120100, 120105 | standard |
| DBM-Raids-Midnight | 120100, 120105 | standard |
| DBM-Lairs-Midnight | 120100, 120105 | standard |

DBM-Core also bundles libraries with their own TOCs (`DBM-Core/Libs/LibStub` 90005, `LibDropDownMenu` with a multi-client list, `LibCustomGlow-1.0` 120001/120000). They are nested inside DBM-Core, not addon roots.

**BigWigs** (`gh:BigWigsMods/BigWigs`, `BigWigs-v427.6.zip`; release.json flavors `mainline:120100/120105/120007, classic:11508/11509, bcc:20505/20506, wrath:30405, titan:38002, cata:40402, mists:50503/50504, forever:16001`):

- Shared: `BigWigs`, `BigWigs_Core`, `BigWigs_Options`, `BigWigs_Plugins`, each listing every client's interface.
- Retail-only, `## Interface: 120100, 120105, 120007` and `## AllowLoadGameType: standard`: `BigWigs_TheVoidspire`, `BigWigs_TheDreamrift`, `BigWigs_MarchOnQuelDanas`, `BigWigs_MidnightWorld`, `BigWigs_Sporefall`, `BigWigs_TheVenomousAbyss`, `BigWigs_MidnightLairs`, `BigWigs_TheUnbindingOfKithix`.

The M1 checkpoint misread this bug. It installed DBM 12.1.14 and BigWigs v427.6 on retail, recorded their refusal on the synthetic Forever target as "no Forever build before launch", and ticked the item. Both releases already declared `forever:16001`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On a machine with a Classic Era client (or a synthetic one): `omaddons install dbm bigwigs -t era --dry-run --json`.
2. Both items fail with `no_compatible_release`: "gh:DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods: no candidate loads on this client (era on vanilla)", with the tried candidate's reason `wrong_flavor: DBM-Brawlers: {"verdict":"wrong_flavor","reason":"game_type_excluded"}; ...`.
3. Same result with `-t anniversary` (tbc), `-t classic` (mists) and `-t forever` (forever).
4. `curl -sL https://github.com/DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods/releases/latest/download/release.json` lists the target's flavor for that very file.
5. Retail installs both, because every folder loads there.

## Technical Approach

Separate two questions that `compatible()` answers together: **is this candidate meant for this client**, and **which of its folders does this client load**.

1. **Partition the verdicts.** Add a function next to `verify()` in `src/engine/inspect.rs` that splits `Vec<FolderVerdict>` into `install` (verdict `Compatible`) and `skip` (verdict `WrongFlavor`, carrying the `WrongFlavorReason`).
2. **Dependency closure.** A `Compatible` folder whose loaded TOC requires (`Dependencies`, `RequiredDeps`, any `Dep*` directive) a folder that is skipped from the same archive would not load either. Move it to `skip` with reason `dependency_skipped { folder }`, and repeat until stable. Use the parsed TOC from `LoadedTocSummary`/the TOC module; do not re-parse.
3. **Acceptance rule.** Accept the candidate when `install` is non-empty and:
   - **(a) Publisher declared the target.** `candidate.rank` is `MetadataInterface` or `MetadataFlavor` (release.json matched this client in `src/resolve/select.rs`). Skipped folders are then any `WrongFlavor` folders.
   - **(b) No metadata** (git, url, local zip or dir, REST asset lists, name hints: `NameHint`, `Unannotated`, and the mismatch tiers). The addon's primary folder must be in `install`. Pick it the way `addon_name()` in `src/engine/plan.rs` names the addon: repo-named folder, else the folder others extend, else the core folder, else the shortest. Also, every skipped folder must be excluded by an explicit per-folder gate: `GameTypeExcluded` (AllowLoadGameType/ExcludeLoadGameType) or `NoLoadableToc` (only flavor-suffixed TOCs for other clients). If a skipped folder is merely `InterfaceNotInFamily` or `NoInterface`, keep today's strict refusal. That keeps "a retail-only zip whose bundled library happens to load on Classic" refused.
   - Otherwise refuse as today, with the per-folder reasons in `tried[].reason`.
4. **Plan only installed folders.** `build_install()` builds `new_folders` from `inspected.folders`. Build it from the `install` set instead, so stage, ownership, swap ops, the addon record's `folders`, the files index and snapshots only ever see folders that are written. Skipped folders are never extracted to the client. Staging may still extract them to the stage dir if that is simpler, but they must not reach `Interface/AddOns`.
5. **Updates.** A folder installed by an earlier release that a newer release now skips falls into `dropped` and is removed, as today. Add a test for it.
6. **Ownership.** If a skipped folder already exists on disk and is unmanaged (copied by hand or by another manager), leave it untouched and unclaimed. `status` keeps counting it as `invalid`.
7. **Output (additive contract change).**
   - The install item's `folders` object gains `skipped: [{ "name": "DBM-Midnight", "reason": "game_type_excluded" }]`, next to `added`/`replaced`/`removed`.
   - Human output adds one line per addon: `skipped 4 folders this client does not load: DBM-Brawlers, DBM-Midnight, DBM-Raids-Midnight, DBM-Lairs-Midnight`.
   - Update the contract snapshots and the JSON schema.
8. **Docs.** In README.md "Installs what loads", add: "Folders in a multi-client archive that this client would not load are skipped and listed."

## Acceptance Criteria

- `omaddons install dbm -t era|anniversary|classic|forever --dry-run --json` resolves the current DBM-Core release:
  - `folders.added` is DBM-Core, DBM-GUI, DBM-StatusBarTimers and DBM-VPVEM;
  - `folders.skipped` is DBM-Brawlers, DBM-Midnight, DBM-Raids-Midnight and DBM-Lairs-Midnight, each with `game_type_excluded`.
- BigWigs likewise adds its 4 shared folders and skips its 8 retail-only modules on the same four clients.
- On retail, DBM and BigWigs still install every folder and skip none.
- A no-metadata archive where only a bundled library folder loads on the target is still refused with `no_compatible_release`.
- WeakAuras 5.22.1 is still refused on retail and forever, since its release.json declares neither.
- A folder that depends on a skipped folder is skipped with `dependency_skipped`.
- Skipped folders never appear under `Interface/AddOns`, in the addon record, in the files index or in a snapshot.
- Undo restores the AddOns folder byte for byte.
- After installing DBM and BigWigs into a Classic target, `status` reports 0 invalid folders for it.
- An update whose new release skips a previously installed folder removes that folder, and undo restores it.
- `argc gate` passes, with contract snapshots updated.

## Test Plan

- **Unit** (`src/engine/inspect.rs` tests):
  - partition cases: all compatible; mixed with metadata; mixed without metadata (primary compatible, skips gated); library-only compatible (refused); `InterfaceNotInFamily` skip without metadata (refused); transitive dependency skip; nothing compatible (refused);
  - a proptest that `install ∪ skip` equals the inspected folders and that the two sets are disjoint.
- **Fixture E2E** (`tests/install.rs` or `tests/plan.rs`, HTTP replay under `tests/fixtures/http`):
  - DBM-shaped and BigWigs-shaped archives built from the folder names and TOC header lines above, with stub Lua files and a release.json declaring the flavors above;
  - install into synthetic retail, era, anniversary, classic, forever and titan targets;
  - assert `added`/`skipped`, the on-disk folder set, `status` invalid = 0, and that undo restores the folder.
- **TOC matrix** (`tests/toc_matrix.rs`): rows for `## AllowLoadGameType: standard` on every family. `game_type_excluded` everywhere except mainline, where it is `compatible`.
- **Update E2E:** release N installs folder X; release N+1 gates X to retail; update on era removes X; undo restores it.
- **Contract:** install success envelope snapshot with `folders.skipped`.
- **Live** (`tests/live_probes.rs`, ignored): real DBM and BigWigs into synthetic era, anniversary, classic and forever targets. The catalog-wide probe bead covers the rest.

## Considerations

- **Keep the WeakAuras guarantee** ("never installs a wrong-flavor build"). Selection still prefers the release.json entry for the target. This change applies only after a candidate is chosen for that client.
- **Game types.** Forever's game type is `camelot`, so `AllowLoadGameType: standard` correctly excludes it. Do not special-case Forever.
- **Rank tiers.** If `MetadataMismatch` or `NameHintMismatch` candidates are tried at all, rule (b) applies to them, never rule (a).
- **Archive limits** are unchanged: skipped folders were already inspected under the same limits.
- **Bundled libraries.** Nested `Libs/*.toc` files are not roots and need no change. Re-check `find_roots` with the DBM layout so `DBM-Core/Libs/LibStub` never becomes a root.
- **Watch the contract.** Agents may already parse `folders`; adding `skipped` is additive.
acceptance_criteria: DBM and BigWigs install on era, anniversary, classic and forever with their shared folders added and retail-only modules listed in folders.skipped (game_type_excluded); retail installs every folder; a no-metadata archive where only a bundled library loads is still refused; WeakAuras still refused where release.json does not declare the client; folders depending on a skipped folder are skipped (dependency_skipped); skipped folders never reach Interface/AddOns, the record, the files index or snapshots; undo restores byte for byte; status shows 0 invalid after install; an update that newly skips a folder removes it and undo restores it; argc gate passes with contract snapshots updated
close_reason: Multi-client archives now install the folders the client loads and list the rest in folders.skipped. inspect.rs: partition() splits verdicts (dependency closure via dependency_skipped) and accepts() applies rule (a) release.json-declared vs rule (b) primary folder loads and every skip is gated. plan.rs keeps only loadable folders in the staged Inspected and carries skipped through AddonWork so rejudge under the lock reports it too.

comments.author: RustyDolphin
comments.text: claim: src/engine/inspect.rs, src/engine/plan.rs, src/output (install folders.skipped), tests/install*, tests/toc_matrix.rs, contract snapshots, README

comments.author: RustyDolphin
comments.text: done: argc gate passes (47 suites); new tests/install_multi_flavor.rs: DBM- and BigWigs-shaped releases on era, anniversary, classic, forever, titan and retail (added/skipped, on-disk set, status managed=N unmanaged=0 invalid=0, skipped names absent from client and state, undo byte-identical), no-metadata rule (b) refusals and gated install with dependency_skipped, WeakAuras still refused on retail and forever, update that newly skips a folder removes it and undo restores it; unit tests and a proptest for partition/accepts; 8 TOC matrix rows for AllowLoadGameType standard; live probe boss_mods_install_their_shared_folders_on_classic_and_forever passes against DBM 12.1.14 and BigWigs v427.6 (4 shared added, 4/8 skipped game_type_excluded on every non-retail client, none on retail); existing Forever live probe now installs DBM and BigWigs and still refuses WeakAuras 5.22.1. decided: status has no invalid-addon count, so 'status 0 invalid' is checked as targets[].folders invalid=0 and unmanaged=0 · found: none

title: Install into a never-launched client (no Interface/AddOns) fails with a false retryable plan_stale
description:
## Background

A WoW client creates `Interface/AddOns` on its first launch. Until then the folder does not exist. That covers every freshly installed client: Battle.net, Steam, Lutris, Heroic and Bottles prefixes, and custom private-server clients. Right now it also covers the development machine's real Forever stress-test client (`_forever_`, `wowf`, 1.60.1.70245), which cannot launch before 2026-10-19 and has neither `Interface/` nor `WTF/`.

Discovery already handles this state: `status` lists the target, and `list` reports `addons_dir_missing: true` ("no AddOns folder yet"). Install does not. `Target::addons_dir()` in `src/model.rs` is documented "Produced here, never created here", and nothing else creates it:

1. Swap-in renames staged folders into `<client>/Interface/AddOns/<Folder>`.
2. fsx `normalize()` in `src/fsx/mutate.rs` canonicalizes the parent. A missing parent becomes `FsxError::Precondition("the parent of … does not exist")`.
3. `try_flagged()` in `src/engine/swap.rs` maps a `Precondition` during `SwapIn` to `plan_stale`, "… changed after planning", with `retryable: true`.

The error is false twice over: nothing changed after planning, and retrying fails the same way every time. `--dry-run` does not reach the swap, so it reports `status: installed` for an install that cannot succeed.

## Steps to Reproduce

Reproduced 2026-10-15 in a throwaway HOME, with the real client untouched:

1. Make a temp dir `T`. Copy a Battle.net `.build.info` and `.product.db` that list `wowf` into `T/Games/battlenet/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft/`. Create `_forever_/Wow.exe` there as an empty file; there is no `Interface/`.
2. Point `HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME` and `XDG_CACHE_HOME` into `T`.
3. `omaddons status --json` shows `forever` (family forever, interface 16001).
4. `omaddons install plater -t forever --dry-run --json` returns `ok: true`, with Plater `status: installed`.
5. `omaddons install plater -t forever --json` exits 1 with `plan_stale`: "<client>/Interface/AddOns/Plater changed after planning: the parent of <client>/Interface/AddOns/Plater does not exist". It is marked `retryable: true`.
6. Run it again: the same error, every time.
7. `omaddons undo` says "nothing to undo". On disk, `Interface/.omaddons/{target.json,stage,snapshots,trash}` exist and `Interface/AddOns` does not.

## Technical Approach

1. **Create the AddOns folder inside the transaction.** After taking the target lock and before the first swap-in step, create `Interface/AddOns` (and `Interface` if missing) through fsx `ensure_dir_all` in the transaction's write session. That respects the one-writer rule: no direct `std::fs`. Mode 0755.
2. **Journal it.** Record the creation as a journal step (e.g. a new `StepOp::EnsureDir`, or a `created_dirs` list on the transaction record), so crash recovery and history know omaddons made it.
   - Recovery after a crash before any swap-in may leave the empty folder in place, because the client would create it anyway.
   - Recovery must never leave staged content in `Interface/AddOns`.
3. **Undo semantics.** Undo removes the installed addon folders and leaves `Interface/AddOns` in place, even when empty. Reasons:
   - the client creates the same folder on first launch;
   - an empty AddOns folder is inert;
   - removing it could race a client that has since launched.
   Record this as a `decided:` comment on the bead when closing.
4. **Look for case variants first.** On a case-sensitive filesystem a user or tool may have created `interface/addons`. Wine resolves paths case-insensitively, so creating a second `Interface/AddOns` beside it would leave two folders, only one of which the game reads.
   - Before creating, look for a case-insensitive match of `Interface` and `AddOns`. If one exists, use it.
   - If two variants exist, refuse with a safety error that names both paths (exit 4).
   - `addons_dir()` may need to become a resolving function, or stay pure with a resolver beside it. Keep `list`/`status` consistent with whatever the engine uses.
5. **Plan and dry-run.** The plan records `creates_addons_dir: true` when the folder is missing at plan time.
   - The install data envelope gains `creates_addons_dir` (additive contract field).
   - The human output says "creating Interface/AddOns (this client has not been launched yet)".
   - Dry-run and the real run report the same thing.
6. **Narrow `plan_stale`.** After this fix, a missing parent during swap-in means the folder vanished after the transaction created it, which is genuine staleness, so keep `plan_stale` for it. Audit the other `Precondition`→`plan_stale` paths in `src/engine/swap.rs` for deterministic failures that would claim `retryable: true` falsely. Mark any such path non-retryable or give it its own code.
7. **Marker order.** The target marker `Interface/.omaddons/target.json` is written on first mutation and already creates `Interface/`. Make sure the AddOns creation does not depend on the marker having run first.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Install into a client with `Interface/` but no `AddOns/` succeeds: it creates `Interface/AddOns`, installs the addon, and passes TOC verification.
- Install into a client with no `Interface/` at all succeeds the same way.
- `--dry-run` reports `creates_addons_dir: true` and says so in human output; the real run reports the same; neither reports success for an install that then fails.
- Undo of that first install removes the addon folders and leaves an empty `Interface/AddOns`; `history` shows the transaction.
- When the folder only exists under a different case (`interface/addons`), that folder is used and no second one is created. When two case variants exist, install refuses with a safety error naming both.
- A crash injected at every step of a first install into a missing AddOns folder recovers to "no addon folders" or "addon fully installed", never to a partial folder or staged leftovers in `Interface/AddOns`.
- No deterministic failure is reported with `retryable: true`.
- `argc gate` passes, with contract snapshots updated.

## Test Plan

- **E2E** (`tests/install.rs`): synthetic clients (Battle.net flavor folder, custom client) with no `Interface/` and with `Interface/` but no `AddOns/`. Install a fixture addon; assert the folders exist, the addon is installed, and `creates_addons_dir` is in JSON and human output; then run `--dry-run` on a fresh copy and assert it matches.
- **Undo** (`tests/engine_undo.rs`): undo leaves an empty `Interface/AddOns`, and history lists the transaction.
- **Crash** (`tests/engine_crash.rs`): extend the crash matrix with a first install into a missing AddOns folder, a failpoint at every step, and recovery to one side.
- **Case variants** (`tests/engine_fallbacks.rs` or `tests/install.rs`): lowercase `interface/addons` is reused; two variants are refused.
- **Contract:** dry-run and install envelope snapshots include the new field.
- **Real machine:** the Forever real-client bead runs the real case before the client's first launch.

## Considerations

- `inventory` and `list` already model `addons_dir_missing`. Reuse that rather than probing again.
- Steam/Lutris prefixes are often on other filesystems (ext4, ntfs3). Creating a directory must not assume reflink or `RENAME_EXCHANGE` support.
- Scope rules in `src/fsx/scope.rs` must allow creating `Interface` and `Interface/AddOns` under a target's client dir, but nothing above it.
- The fix must not touch `Blizzard_*` protection or ownership: an empty new folder has no folders to protect.
acceptance_criteria: Install into a client with no Interface/ or no Interface/AddOns creates the folder and installs; dry-run reports creates_addons_dir and agrees with the real run; undo removes addon folders and leaves an empty Interface/AddOns; an existing case variant (interface/addons) is reused and two variants are refused with a safety error; a crash at every step of a first install recovers to one side with no staged leftovers; no deterministic failure is reported retryable; argc gate passes with contract snapshots updated
close_reason: First installs into a never-launched client create Interface/AddOns inside the transaction: the commit window records creates_dirs in the journal's prepared line, then creates the folder through fsx before the first swap; plan, dry run and real run report creates_addons_dir; undo leaves the empty folder. ClientPaths resolves an existing case variant (interface/addons) for every engine path; two spellings are refused with case_collision (exit 4, not retryable) at plan and under the lock.

title: Game-mode names: -t sod and -t hardcore select the Classic Era client; status lists the modes each client runs
description:
## Background

Battle.net runs three Classic game modes from one client. Classic Era, Hardcore and Season of Discovery all launch from the "Classic" entry in the launcher and run `_classic_era_` (product `wow_classic_era`, 1.15.9, interface 11509, family vanilla).

Verified on the development machine on 2026-10-15:
- `.build.info` lists exactly five products: `wow`, `wowf`, `wow_classic`, `wow_classic_era`, `wow_anniversary`. There is no separate Hardcore or SoD product.
- Booting Era, Hardcore and SoD in turn wrote three realm folders under `_classic_era_/WTF/Account/<account>/`.
- Mists of Pandaria Classic is `wow_classic` in `_classic_` (5.5.4, 50504, mists).
- Burning Crusade Anniversary is `wow_anniversary` in `_anniversary_` (2.5.6, 20506, tbc).

All three modes in `_classic_era_` share one `Interface/AddOns`, so an addon installed for one is installed for all three.

Players think in modes ("I play SoD"), but omaddons names clients only by default id (`era`), product, flavor folder, family or path. Target resolution (`resolve()` in `src/discover/registry.rs`) tries, in order: target key, id, product code, flavor folder, family, path. So:
- `omaddons install questie -t sod` and `-t hardcore` fail with `target_not_found`;
- `status` labels the client "era (battlenet)" and never mentions Hardcore or Season of Discovery;
- a new user cannot tell where their mode went, or that the three modes share addons.

## Technical Approach

1. **Mode table as data** (vision D15). Extend the `Product` rows in `src/rules.rs` (`PRODUCTS`, `builtin_products()`) with `modes: Vec<GameMode>`, where `GameMode { id, name, aliases }`:

   | Product | Modes (id: name; aliases) |
   |---|---|
   | `wow_classic_era` | `classic-era`: Classic Era (none); `hardcore`: Hardcore (`hc`); `sod`: Season of Discovery (`season-of-discovery`) |
   | `wow_classic` | `mists-classic`: Mists of Pandaria Classic (`mop`, `mop-classic`) |
   | `wow_anniversary` | `tbc-anniversary`: Burning Crusade Anniversary (`bc-anniversary`) |
   | `wow` | `retail`: Retail (none) |
   | `wowf` | `forever`: WoW: Forever (none) |

   Test, PTR and beta products get no modes.

2. **Collision rule.** No mode id or alias may equal a default target id (`retail`, `classic`, `era`, `anniversary`, `forever`, `ptr`, `xptr`, `beta`, `classic-ptr`, `classic-beta`, `era-ptr`, `titan`), a family name (`vanilla`, `tbc`, `wotlk`, `cata`, `mists` and the `*-legacy` names), or a product code. That is why `mists` and `tbc` are not aliases here: they already resolve by family, and legacy custom clients take those names.
   - Where a mode id equals the default id of its own product (`retail`, `forever`), resolving by id already wins, so the mode is display-only.
   - A rules-table unit test enforces the collision rule.
3. **Resolution.** In `resolve()`, add a step after the flavor-folder step and before the family step: a case-insensitive match of a mode id or alias selects the targets whose product hosts that mode.
   - Explicit ids still win, because step 2 runs first, so a registered target named `sod` keeps working.
   - When several clients host the mode (a Steam and a Battle.net Classic Era install), the existing `target_ambiguous` path applies, listing every candidate.
4. **Not installed.** When a mode alias matches the table but no discovered target hosts it, `target_not_found` says so, e.g. "Season of Discovery runs in the Classic Era client (`_classic_era_`), which was not found on this machine". `fix`: `omaddons targets --rescan`.
5. **Output (additive contract).**
   - `status --json` and `targets --json` targets gain `modes: [{ "id": "sod", "name": "Season of Discovery" }, …]`.
   - The human `status` and `targets` line for a multi-mode client reads e.g. `era  Classic Era · Hardcore · Season of Discovery  1.15.9`.
   - `install -t sod` adds a note (not a warning) that the addons go to `era`, which Classic Era and Hardcore share.
6. **Help and docs.**
   - `omaddons help install` (and every `-t` help line) mentions that game-mode names work.
   - README.md's target id paragraph gains "Season of Discovery and Hardcore run in the Classic Era client: `-t sod` and `-t hardcore` select `era`."
7. **Vision.** Add a comment on omad-vision-8qa recording the mode table and that it was verified on 2026-10-15.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `omaddons install <addon> -t sod`, `-t SoD`, `-t season-of-discovery`, `-t hardcore` and `-t hc` all resolve to the Classic Era target; `-t mop` resolves to `classic`; `-t tbc-anniversary` resolves to `anniversary`.
- `status --json` lists `modes` for era (3), classic (1) and anniversary (1); human `status` shows the mode names on the era line.
- A registered target whose id is `sod` takes precedence over the alias.
- With no Classic Era client, `-t sod` fails `target_not_found` with a message naming the Classic Era client and `fix_argv` `["omaddons","targets","--rescan"]`.
- The rules-table test proves no mode id or alias collides with a default id, family name or product code.
- `install -t sod` output notes that the addons are shared with Classic Era and Hardcore.
- `argc gate` passes; contract snapshots (status, targets, install, help) are updated.

## Test Plan

- **Unit** (`src/rules.rs`): table invariants (aliases unique, lowercase, valid as ids, no collisions); every live Classic product has at least one mode.
- **Unit** (`src/discover/registry.rs`): resolution order (an id beats a mode alias, a mode alias beats a family); an ambiguous mode across two Classic Era installs gives `target_ambiguous` with both ids.
- **E2E** (`tests/targets.rs`, `tests/discover_matrix.rs`): a synthetic Battle.net tree with `_classic_era_`, `_classic_`, `_anniversary_`; `install x -t sod --dry-run --json` names target `era`; status snapshot shows modes; a missing-client case shows the not-found message.
- **Contract:** status/targets envelopes and help text snapshots.
- **Real machine:** the Classic real-client bead asserts `modes` and `-t sod`/`-t hardcore` on the development machine.

## Considerations

- Blizzard moves modes between clients: Anniversary realms ran in the Classic Era client from November 2024 until TBC Anniversary moved to `_anniversary_`. The table is data with a verification date; when it changes, a comment on the vision records it.
- Mode-specific addons (SoD rune trackers, Hardcore death alerts) decide at runtime through game APIs, not through TOC rules. No TOC change is needed, and per-mode addon sets are a non-goal because the game shares the folder.
- Keep aliases few. Every alias is a name the contract must keep after the freeze (M4).
- The realm folders under `WTF/` could reveal which modes a player uses, but reading them is out of scope; `WTF/` is M3's backup territory.
acceptance_criteria: -t sod, SoD, season-of-discovery, hardcore and hc resolve to era; -t mop to classic; -t tbc-anniversary to anniversary; status --json lists modes for era (3), classic and anniversary and human status shows them; a registered target id beats a mode alias; with no Classic Era client -t sod fails target_not_found naming the Classic Era client with fix_argv omaddons targets --rescan; a rules-table test proves no alias collides with a default id, family name or product code; install -t sod notes the shared folder; argc gate passes with snapshots updated
close_reason: Game-mode names select the client that runs them: a mode table on the product rows (src/rules.rs, validated against product codes, default ids and family names), a mode step in resolve() between flavor folder and family, target_not_found naming the missing client, modes in status/targets JSON and human output, an install note when -t names a shared mode, the -t help line and README.

title: Real-machine smoke tests for the Classic Era, Anniversary and Mists Classic clients
description:
## Background

The M1 checkpoint's real-machine tests in `tests/real_machine.rs` cover two clients:
- `status_reports_retail_and_335` asserts only the retail and 3.3.5a targets;
- `keyless_installs_retail` and `legacy_installs_335_from_git_and_from_a_release` install into those two only.

Since 2026-10-15 the development machine also has every live Classic client, each booted once so `Interface/AddOns` exists (empty):

| Target id | Product | Version | Interface | Family | Modes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `era` | `wow_classic_era` | 1.15.9.70003 | 11509 | vanilla | Classic Era, Hardcore, Season of Discovery |
| `anniversary` | `wow_anniversary` | 2.5.6.70006 | 20506 | tbc | Burning Crusade Anniversary |
| `classic` | `wow_classic` | 5.5.4.70268 | 50504 | mists | Mists of Pandaria Classic |

Dry-runs on 2026-10-15 against these real clients:
- WeakAuras 5.22.1, Questie (`bundle/v12.1.0+v1.0.6`, upstream's own tag), Bartender4 4.18.3.1 and OmniCC 11.2.8 resolved on all three;
- DBM and BigWigs were refused (the multi-flavor archive bug in this epic).

No test has ever installed into a real Classic client.

## Technical Approach

Extend `tests/real_machine.rs`. Keep its existing protocol:
- every test is `#[ignore]`, gated on `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE=1`, and also `OMADDONS_LIVE=1` when it touches the network;
- it uses the real HOME and XDG dirs;
- it records each touched AddOns folder's tree hash before it starts;
- it undoes every transaction it made, newest first, and only then asserts that the hashes are unchanged (the lesson from the checkpoint run that left installs behind).

1. **Status.** Rename `status_reports_retail_and_335` to `status_reports_every_client`, keeping the retail and 3.3.5a asserts. Add, for era, anniversary and classic:
   - `product`, `family`, `interface` and `kind: live`;
   - the version prefix (`1.15.`, `2.5.`, `5.5.`);
   - `running: false` (skip the assert with a note if the client is running);
   - no `attention` items;
   - `folders.invalid == 0`.
   Look targets up by family with the existing `target(&status, family)` helper.
2. **Modes** (after the game-mode bead): assert `modes` for era (Classic Era, Hardcore, Season of Discovery), that `-t sod` and `-t hardcore` resolve to `era`, and that `-t mop` resolves to `classic` (use `install … --dry-run --json` and read `data.target`).
3. **Installs.** New test `keyless_installs_classic` (`OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE=1 OMADDONS_LIVE=1`). For each of `era`, `anniversary` and `classic`:
   - install `weakauras dbm bigwigs questie bartender4 omnicc` in one command;
   - assert every item `installed`, with TOC verification passing and the expected folders: DBM adds 4 and skips 4 retail modules, BigWigs adds 4 and skips 8;
   - assert `status` shows 0 invalid folders and the new managed count;
   - log each resolved version with `note()` for the close reason;
   - undo every transaction, newest first;
   - assert each AddOns tree hash equals its pre-test value.
4. **Undo across clients.** Assert that undoing in one client never touches another client's AddOns (hash all three before and after each undo).
5. **SavedVariables safety.** The clients have `WTF/` from their first boot. Assert that `WTF/` hashes are unchanged by install and undo, since nothing here should write `WTF/`.
6. **Docs.** Update the "real-machine" line in README.md's local gate section if the test names change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE=1 OMADDONS_LIVE=1 cargo test --test real_machine -- --ignored --test-threads=1` passes on the development machine, including `status_reports_every_client` and `keyless_installs_classic`.
- All six addons install and verify on era, anniversary and classic. DBM and BigWigs report their skipped retail-only folders.
- Every AddOns folder and every `WTF/` tree is hash-identical to its pre-test state after the run.
- The game-mode assertions (`modes`, `-t sod`, `-t hardcore`, `-t mop`) pass.
- The close reason records, per client, each addon's resolved version and folder counts.
- `argc gate` passes. The tests are ignored by default, so the gate's run is unchanged.

## Test Plan

- This bead is itself a test. Run it twice in a row to prove it is idempotent and leaves no state that changes the second run.
- Run `status_reports_every_client` alone without `OMADDONS_LIVE` to confirm it needs no network.
- Negative check: temporarily point it at a missing client (rename the expected family in a local edit, not committed) to confirm the failure message names the missing target clearly; revert the edit.

## Considerations

- Close every game client before running; the running policy would otherwise refuse or defer changes.
- Publishers republish often. Assert folder names and skip counts by pattern (retail-only modules carry `AllowLoadGameType: standard`), not exact versions.
- If a publisher drops a Classic flavor from release.json, the test must fail with a message naming the publisher and flavor, not a bare assert.
- Live network: GitHub keyless only; no REST on the stable channel, per the existing zero-REST assertion pattern.
acceptance_criteria: status_reports_every_client and keyless_installs_classic pass on the development machine under OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE=1 OMADDONS_LIVE=1; weakauras, dbm, bigwigs, questie, bartender4 and omnicc install and verify on era, anniversary and classic with DBM/BigWigs skips reported; every AddOns and WTF tree is hash-identical after the run; mode assertions (modes, -t sod, -t hardcore, -t mop) pass; close reason records versions and folder counts per client; argc gate passes
close_reason: tests/real_machine.rs: status_reports_every_client now asserts era, anniversary and classic (product, interface, kind live, version prefix, no attention, 0 invalid; running noted) plus the era modes and -t sod/-t hardcore/-t mop selection, with no network; new keyless_installs_classic installs weakauras dbm bigwigs questie bartender4 omnicc into each real Classic client, records everything, undoes newest first, then asserts: each publisher still declares the client's flavor (message names publisher and flavor), every item installed, DBM/BigWigs add their core folder and skip only game_type_excluded modules, status managed equals the folders added and invalid 0, each undo restores its client and leaves the others as they were, every AddOns and WTF tree hash-identical after, zero REST since the test began. keyless_installs_forever now skips while the forever client manages addons (the stress-test set stays installed per xud.6).

title: Real-machine smoke tests for the real Forever stress-test client
description:
## Background

The M1 checkpoint proved WoW: Forever only against a synthetic target (`live_probes::keyless_installs_into_a_synthetic_forever_target`). The development machine now has the real Forever stress-test client, installed 2026-10-15:

- folder `_forever_` under the Battle.net root; product `wowf`; version 1.60.1.70245; interface 16001; family forever;
- `_forever_` holds `Wow.exe`, `wow_loader.dll`, `D3D12/` and `UTILS/`, but no `Interface/` and no `WTF/`, because it has never been launched;
- the stress test opens 2026-10-19 and Forever launches 2026-11-04.

Dry-runs against the real client on 2026-10-15:
- Plater (Plater-v661) and Bartender4 (4.18.3.1) resolve;
- DBM and BigWigs are refused (the multi-flavor archive bug), although both declare `forever:16001`;
- WeakAuras 5.22.1 is correctly refused, because its release.json declares no `forever` flavor.

A real install fails, because the client has no `Interface/AddOns` (the never-launched client bug). Questie also declares `forever:16001` and has not been tried.

## Technical Approach

Extend `tests/real_machine.rs` with the same protocol as the retail and Classic tests:
- `#[ignore]`, gated on `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE=1 OMADDONS_LIVE=1`;
- real HOME and XDG dirs;
- hashes recorded before, every transaction undone newest first, assertions after.

1. **Status.** In `status_reports_every_client`, assert the forever target: `product: wowf`, `family: forever`, `interface: 16001`, version prefix `1.60.`, `kind: live`, and `addons_dir_missing` matching what is on disk.
2. **Installs.** New test `keyless_installs_forever`:
   - **Record the starting state:** whether `Interface/` and `Interface/AddOns` exist, and the AddOns tree hash when they do.
   - **Install** `plater bartender4 dbm bigwigs questie` into `-t forever`. Assert each is `installed` and verified; DBM and BigWigs report their skipped retail-only folders.
   - **Missing folder:** if `Interface/AddOns` was missing, assert the result says it was created (`creates_addons_dir: true`).
   - **WeakAuras:** assert `install weakauras -t forever` fails `no_compatible_release`, unless WeakAuras' release.json now declares `forever`, in which case assert it installs. Log which case held.
   - **Undo** every transaction, newest first.
   - **Restored:** assert the AddOns contents match the starting state. The documented exceptions are an empty `Interface/AddOns`, which stays after undo, and the target marker `Interface/.omaddons/target.json`.
3. **Ordering.** The missing-folder path only exists before the owner's first launch on 2026-10-19. Run this test before then. If the client has already launched, the test still runs; the missing-folder case stays covered by the fixture tests in the never-launched client bug.
4. **Evidence.** Log every resolved version, folder count and skipped list with `note()` for the close reason. Add a comment on omad-wez with the results, so the post-launch re-check starts from real data.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `status_reports_every_client` asserts the real forever target and passes.
- `keyless_installs_forever` passes against the real client:
  - Plater, Bartender4, DBM, BigWigs and Questie install and verify;
  - WeakAuras behaves as its release.json declares;
  - every transaction is undone;
  - AddOns contents match the starting state, apart from the documented exceptions.
- At least one run happens before the client's first launch, and its close-reason evidence shows `creates_addons_dir: true`.
- omad-wez has a comment with the per-publisher results.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- This bead is itself a test. Run it twice; the second run starts with an existing empty `Interface/AddOns` and must also pass.
- Run `status_reports_every_client` alone without `OMADDONS_LIVE` to confirm it needs no network.

## Considerations

- The client must not be running. Wine/Proton process detection applies, as for retail.
- Forever's game type is `camelot`, so retail-only modules gated to `standard` are skipped. Assert the skip reason is `game_type_excluded`.
- Publishers may add or remove `forever` builds before launch. Assert by declared flavor, not a fixed list, and fail with a message naming the publisher.
- Do not leave addons installed here; keeping a set for the stress test is a separate bead.
acceptance_criteria: status_reports_every_client asserts the real forever target (wowf, forever, 16001, 1.60.); keyless_installs_forever installs and verifies plater, bartender4, dbm, bigwigs and questie, checks weakauras against its declared flavors, undoes everything and leaves AddOns as found apart from the documented empty Interface/AddOns and marker; at least one run before the first launch records creates_addons_dir true; omad-wez gets a results comment; argc gate passes
close_reason: tests/real_machine.rs: status_reports_every_client (renamed from status_reports_retail_and_335) asserts the real forever target and that list's addons_dir_missing matches disk; new keyless_installs_forever installs plater, bartender4, dbm, bigwigs and questie into the real client, asserts each installs exactly when its release.json declares forever (via info latest.flavors), that DBM/BigWigs skip retail-only modules as game_type_excluded, that creates_addons_dir is true exactly when AddOns was missing, checks WeakAuras against its declared flavors, undoes everything and asserts AddOns as found (or the created folder left empty).

title: Confirm omaddons-installed addons load in the real Forever client during the 2026-10-19 stress test
description:
## Background

TOC verification proves omaddons installs what the client's rules say should load. It does not prove the real client loads it. No test has observed a Forever client loading an addon installed by omaddons: Forever has never been playable on the development machine.

The owner will play the Forever stress test from 2026-10-19 (the client is installed; see the Forever real-client bead). That session is the first chance to confirm, before the 2026-11-04 launch, that:
- the folder layout, TOC suffixes (`_Forever`/`_Camelot`) and interface 16001 match what the real client accepts;
- skipped retail-only folders (DBM, BigWigs) do not stop the shared folders from loading.

The client writes evidence an agent can read afterwards:
- at logout, each loaded addon that declares `## SavedVariables` gets `WTF/Account/<account>/SavedVariables/<Folder>.lua`;
- each addon declaring `## SavedVariablesPerCharacter` gets a file under `WTF/Account/<account>/<realm>/<character>/SavedVariables/`;
- the client writes `AddOns.txt` per character with each addon's enabled state.

An addon the client did not load never gets a SavedVariables file.

## Technical Approach

1. **Before 2026-10-19** (this bead is ready as soon as the Forever real-client bead closes):
   - install the Forever-capable catalog set into the real client and leave it installed for the session: `omaddons install plater bartender4 dbm bigwigs questie -t forever --actor agent --reason "forever stress test load check"`;
   - record the transaction id and every folder in a bead comment;
   - then `br defer <this> --until 2026-10-20` with a transition comment saying it is waiting for the stress-test session.
2. **After the session** (the bead returns to `br ready` on 2026-10-20):
   - Read the evidence under `_forever_/WTF/`. For each installed addon, check for its SavedVariables file:
     - Plater: `Plater.lua`;
     - Bartender4: `Bartender4.lua`;
     - DBM: `DBM-Core.lua` and others;
     - BigWigs: `BigWigs.lua`;
     - Questie: `Questie.lua`.
     Take the authoritative names from each addon's TOC `## SavedVariables` lines.
   - Check `AddOns.txt` for the installed folders.
   - Check that none of the skipped retail-only folders appear (they were never installed).
   - Run `omaddons status -t forever --json` and record `invalid`, `managed` and `attention`.
   - If `WTF/` does not exist yet (the session has not happened), defer again `--until +3d` with a comment. Do not guess.
3. **Results.**
   - Every installed addon shows load evidence: record it in the close reason and a comment on omad-wez.
   - Any installed addon shows no load evidence after a session (no SavedVariables while others have them): file a bug bead (`--deps discovered-from:<this>`) with the addon, its TOC lines and the evidence. That may mean the TOC rules are wrong for the real client.
4. **Leave them installed.** The addons stay installed after the check; the owner manages them with `omaddons remove`/`undo` like any install. Record this as a `decided:` comment: the owner asked to test with this client, and uninstalling working addons after a session would be surprising.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Before 2026-10-19, the Forever-capable catalog set is installed into the real Forever client, with the transaction id and folders recorded in a comment.
- After a stress-test session, each installed addon's load evidence (SavedVariables file and/or AddOns.txt entry) is recorded in the close reason.
- Any addon without load evidence has its own bug bead with the evidence attached.
- omad-wez has a comment summarising the in-game result.
- `omaddons status -t forever` shows 0 invalid folders and no attention items after the session.

## Test Plan

- Evidence collection only; no code change is expected. If the check shows the TOC rules are wrong, the fix gets its own bug bead with fixture tests.
- Use `ls`/`stat` and read-only file reads. Never write under `WTF/`.

## Considerations

- The account folder name under `WTF/Account/` is personal. Refer to it as `<account>` in every bead comment, never by name.
- Addons without SavedVariables leave no file. Rely on `AddOns.txt` for those, and note that `AddOns.txt` alone shows the client listed the addon, not that it loaded.
- The stress test may wipe or change `WTF/` between sessions, so record the evidence as soon as it is there.
- If the stress test date moves, adjust the deferral with a transition comment; this is waiting on an external event, not on the owner.
acceptance_criteria: Before 2026-10-19 the Forever-capable catalog set is installed into the real Forever client with the transaction id and folders recorded; after a stress-test session each addon's load evidence (SavedVariables file and/or AddOns.txt entry) is recorded in the close reason; any addon without load evidence has its own bug bead with the evidence; omad-wez has a summary comment; status -t forever shows 0 invalid folders and no attention items

title: Live probe: every catalog addon installs on every client its publisher declares, and only there
description:
## Background

The multi-flavor archive bug (DBM and BigWigs refused on every non-retail client) shipped through the M1 checkpoint. Nothing compared omaddons' verdicts with what each publisher declares:
- the checkpoint saw BigWigs v427.6 and DBM 12.1.14 refused on the synthetic Forever target;
- it recorded the refusals as "no Forever build before launch" and ticked the item;
- both releases' `release.json` declared `forever:16001`.

A refusal looks exactly like correct behavior unless something checks it against the source of truth.

The catalog (`catalog/catalog.toml`) has 18 entries:
- **13 keyless GitHub entries**, whose `release.json` declares flavors and interfaces per file: WeakAuras, DBM, BigWigs, LittleWigs, Plater, Bartender4, Questie, OmniCC, Dominos, Masque, RaiderIO, MythicDungeonTools, AllTheThings.
- **5 legacy git entries** with a `families` field: pfUI, PlateBuffer, GroupBulletinBoard, MikScrollingBattleText, InFlight.

Publishers use flavor names that differ from omaddons' families. Questie declares `wrath:38002` for Titan, and the `bcc` flavor covers Anniversary. Mapping must therefore go by interface first and flavor name second, the same way `src/resolve/select.rs` ranks `MetadataInterface` above `MetadataFlavor`.

## Technical Approach

1. **New probe.** Add `catalog_matches_declared_flavors` to `tests/live_probes.rs`: `#[ignore]`, gated on `OMADDONS_LIVE=1`.
2. **Synthetic clients.** Build a synthetic HOME with a Battle.net root holding every live product folder: `_retail_`, `_classic_era_`, `_anniversary_`, `_classic_`, `_classic_titan_`, `_forever_`. Give each a `.build.info` row at the version and interface of the rules table's current row, and an existing `Interface/AddOns`. Add one custom legacy client per legacy family (1.12.1, 2.4.3, 3.3.5a, 4.3.4, 5.4.8), reusing the fixture builders in `tests/common` and `tests/discover_matrix.rs`.
3. **What each publisher declares.** For each GitHub catalog entry:
   - fetch the latest stable `release.json` through omaddons' own source, so the request is logged in `net.log` and the allowlist applies;
   - map every declared `(flavor, interface)` to a family with the rules table, interface first;
   - the result is the entry's declared family set.
4. **Expectations.** For each GitHub entry and each synthetic live client, run `omaddons install <entry> -t <id> --dry-run --json`:
   - **declared family:** the item is `installed`. Skipped folders are allowed; each must carry a reason.
   - **undeclared family:** the item fails `no_compatible_release`.
   - **anything else** is a mismatch. That includes `unsafe_archive`, network errors after one retry, and an install on an undeclared family.
5. **Legacy entries.** Install into the synthetic legacy client of each family listed in `families`, and expect a refusal on the other legacy clients.
6. **Report, then assert.** Print a matrix (entry × client: ✓ installed / · refused as declared / ✗ mismatch with reason) through the test's `note()` output, then assert there are no mismatches. Every mismatch line names the entry, the client, the declared flavors and omaddons' reason, so the failure is self-explanatory.
7. **Network budget.** The run uses keyless endpoints only, with zero REST on the stable channel, asserted from `net.log` as `every_github_entry_resolves_without_rest` does. Downloads go through the blob cache, so one archive is fetched once even though it is tried on several clients.
8. **Make it a standing check.**
   - Add the probe to the checkpoint-only checks list in README.md (the live probes line) and to the vision §7 checkpoint list, via a comment on omad-vision-8qa.
   - The close reason of every later milestone checkpoint must include the matrix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `OMADDONS_LIVE=1 cargo test --test live_probes catalog_matches_declared_flavors -- --ignored` exists and passes once the multi-flavor archive bug is fixed. Run it before that fix too and record that it fails on DBM and BigWigs, proving it catches the bug.
- The printed matrix covers all 13 GitHub entries × 6 live clients and all 5 legacy entries × their legacy clients.
- Each mismatch line names the entry, the client, the declared flavors and the reason.
- `net.log` shows zero `api.github.com` requests during the probe.
- README.md and a vision comment list the probe among the checkpoint-only checks.
- `argc gate` passes. The probe is ignored by default.

## Test Plan

- Run the probe against current releases; paste the matrix into the close reason.
- **Negative proof:** run it on a commit before the multi-flavor fix (or with the fix temporarily reverted locally, not committed) and confirm it reports DBM and BigWigs mismatches on era, anniversary, classic, titan and forever.
- **Unit:** the flavor→family mapping helper used by the probe gets cases for `wrath:38002` (titan), `bcc:20506` (tbc), `classic:11509` (vanilla), `forever:16001`, `mainline:120105`, and an unknown flavor (reported, not assumed).

## Considerations

- Releases change daily. The probe asserts agreement with whatever is current, never fixed versions.
- A publisher may declare a flavor whose files really do not load: a publisher bug. Mark such a cell `publisher_mismatch` with the archive's TOC lines, and do not fail the probe for it. Fail only when omaddons disagrees with a correct declaration. A short allowlist, in the test with a dated comment, records known publisher mismatches.
- Entries without `release.json` (when a publisher drops it) fall back to the REST asset list. The probe should report that as a skipped row, not a failure, so the zero-REST assertion stays meaningful.
- Runtime: about 13 × 6 dry-runs plus the legacy rows. Archive downloads are cached, so a run should take minutes, not tens of minutes.
acceptance_criteria: catalog_matches_declared_flavors exists in tests/live_probes.rs, is ignored by default and gated on OMADDONS_LIVE=1, and passes after the multi-flavor fix while failing on DBM/BigWigs before it; its matrix covers 13 GitHub entries x 6 live clients and 5 legacy entries x their legacy clients; mismatch lines name entry, client, declared flavors and reason; net.log shows zero api.github.com requests; README and a vision comment list it among checkpoint-only checks; argc gate passes

title: git refs: a rev that names nothing says so instead of a bare download 404
description:
## Background

`git:https://github.com/<o>/<r>#<rev>` refs (source-git-github) resolve a named rev through `commits/<rev>.atom`. A 404 there makes the rev a tag fetched by name from `codeload.github.com/<o>/<r>/zip/refs/tags/<rev>`, so a rev that names nothing, or any rev on a private or missing repository, only fails later at the archive download with a generic `http_status` 404. The source-git-github bead's considerations promised that this error says private repositories are not supported in M1; today only the no-rev path (default branch feed 404) says so.

## Technical Approach

- When the codeload download of a `Resolved::Tag` asset answers 404, map it to `not_found` with a message naming the rev and the repository: "no branch, tag or commit named <rev> in <o>/<r>, or the repository is private (private repositories are not supported)".
- The mapping belongs where the download error is built for this asset, keyed on the asset's origin (a git ref with a by-name tag), not on every codeload 404.
- Keep the fix argv pointing at `omaddons help install`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A git ref whose rev names nothing yields `not_found` (exit 3 per the exit table) with the rev, the repository and the private-repository note in the message.
- Other download 404s keep their current `http_status` behavior.

## Test Plan

- Replay: synthetic `o/r` with `commits/nope.atom` 404 and `zip/refs/tags/nope` 404 → `not_found` with the message.
- Replay: a `url:` codeload 404 still reports `http_status`.

## Considerations

- GitHub serves `commits/<tag>.atom` for real tags (verified 2026-10-15), so the by-name tag path is rare in practice: it mostly carries the failure case this bead improves.
acceptance_criteria: A git ref whose rev names nothing yields not_found with the rev, the repository and the private-repository note; other download 404s keep http_status
close_reason: a git rev that names nothing is not_found with the rev, the repository and the private-repository note

title: Epic: M1 — Working slice
description:
## Background

M1 is the working slice of omaddons (vision bead omad-vision-8qa, §7). When it closes, omaddons installs, reinstalls-to-update, removes and undoes addons from keyless GitHub, git, URL and local sources into every discovered target, including WoW: Forever and legacy private-server clients. Everything goes through the final transaction engine and the core CLI contract.

The timing matters. WoW: Forever launches on 2026-11-04. M1 alone delivers keyless Forever support:
- the `release.json` flavor `forever`;
- the `_Forever`/`_Camelot` TOC suffixes;
- the guard against a Forever client loading a retail-only `_Mainline.toc`;
- 1.60.x family detection for both `_forever_` and `_classic_beta_`.

M1 also carries the riskiest engine work (journaled per-folder swaps, recovery, undo), so the beads are ordered to put the Forever-critical path first.

M1 is split into seven area epics:

| Epic | Area |
|---|---|
| E1 | Domain model and CLI contract core (envelope, error registry, exit dictionary, clap skeleton, constants) |
| E2 | fsx single writer, locks and state (paths, Op enum, mutate, prune, locks, schema-versioned state, records, history, config) |
| E3 | Client discovery and target identity (BPSV, product.db, dosdevices, Battle.net and custom roots, scan, launchers, cache, running detection, registry) |
| E4 | ClientRules, TOC engine and folder inventory |
| E5 | Network layer and keyless sources (Http, allowlist, net.log, retry, fixtures, refs, local/url/GitHub/git sources, selection, catalog) |
| E6 | Transaction engine (blob cache, archive inspection, staging, ownership, planning, journal, swap, commit, running policy, undo, retention) |
| E7 | M1 commands, the contract conformance suite, fuzzing and checkpoint verification |

## Goals

- Every installed WoW client is discovered with no configuration. Each gets a stable target identity: a ULID key, a human id and a marker.
- Addons install from keyless sources and are verified against the client's own TOC load rules (`ClientRules`). Wrong-flavor builds never install.
- Every mutation is a journaled transaction that is crash-recoverable and undoable, with the "wholly old or wholly new" folder invariant.
- The core CLI contract holds for every M1 command:
  - one stdout envelope under `--json`, on success and on failure;
  - `fix` plus `fix_argv` on every error;
  - NDJSON on stderr when stderr is not a TTY;
  - the general exit dictionary (0–6).
- Privacy is verifiable: a host allowlist checked on every redirect hop, `net.log` covering HTTP and git subprocesses, and `--offline`.

## Success Criteria

All seven area epics are closed, and every M1 checkpoint from the vision is met with recorded evidence (the m1-checkpoint bead under E7 runs them):
- On the development machine, `omaddons status --json` reports `retail` (12.1.x, from `product.db` and `.build.info`) and the 3.3.5a target (`wrath-legacy`, interface 30300, label "localhost", 23 protected folders). Both get stable keys and markers on their first mutation.
- Synthetic trees resolve correctly for:
  - every product, including `_forever_` and `_classic_beta_` at 1.60.x;
  - every legacy `ClientRules` row;
  - a game on a mapped drive letter outside `drive_c`;
  - a custom client outside any prefix;
  - each launcher config;
  - an unknown `_xyz_` folder.
- TOC load-rule tests cover every suffix, the Forever-loads-`_Mainline` case, comma Interface lists and every legacy row.
- Keyless installs of WeakAuras, DBM, BigWigs, Plater and Bartender4 into real retail and a synthetic Forever target are TOC-verified. A legacy addon installs into 3.3.5a from git and from a GitHub release. `Blizzard_*` folders are untouched.
- Installing `release.json` publishers on the stable channel makes zero GitHub REST requests (asserted from `net.log`).
- Failure injection at every engine step leaves each folder wholly old or wholly new. Recovery happens only under the lock, and a reader during a live swap reports `tx_in_progress`.
- Two concurrent installs into one target both complete without `locked`. Lock hold time per commit is under 50 ms.
- `undo` restores folders byte-for-byte, follows the SavedVariables policy, raises `undo_conflict` across transaction kinds, and `--last-by agent` reverts only that actor's transaction.
- The hostile archive suite is rejected, and `blizzard_auctionui/` beside `Blizzard_AuctionUI/` is refused.
- Non-allowlisted hosts fail with `host_blocked`. `net.log` has every request and no credentials.
- The contract core checks pass, the local gate passes, and each fuzz target runs for at least 10 minutes without crashes.
- README.md describes exactly what exists.

## Non-Goals

- `outdated`/`update --all`, WoWInterface and Tukui sources, dependency resolution, adoption, drift checks, `export`/`sync`/`copy` and `search` belong to M2. In M1, `--no-deps` is accepted and ignored.
- The Omarchy widget, `errors` (BugGrabber), `backup` and `--progress json` streams for long operations belong to M3.
- `capabilities`, `robot-docs`, intent inference beyond the closest-command fix, the wire-name golden test, stored plans (`plan_id`, `apply`) and the `doctor` surface belong to M4. M1 ships the engine-guarding warnings (`journal_pending`, `state_version_older`/`state_version_newer`) as plain warnings.
- CurseForge, Wago and release engineering belong to M5.

## Considerations

- The Forever launch layout (`wowf`/`_forever_`/16001) is pre-launch data. Detection is data-driven (D15), and fixtures cover both the beta and launch layouts.
- `product.db` field layout and Proton process naming are UNVERIFIED. Both have fallbacks, and a miss degrades to scanning or a warning, never to data loss.
- Decisions made while decomposing M1 (DEC-1 to DEC-16) are recorded as a comment on omad-vision-8qa. They include these contract additions: errors `scope_denied` and `state_too_new`, and warnings `state_version_older` and `state_version_newer`.
- Parallel agents share one working tree on `main`. The module skeleton and the up-front `Cargo.toml` dependencies exist to keep edits from colliding. Each command bead adds its own clap subcommand.
acceptance_criteria: All seven M1 area epics (E1-E7) are closed; every M1 checkpoint from the vision is met with recorded evidence in the m1-checkpoint bead; the local gate passes; README.md describes exactly what exists
close_reason: All children completed

title: Epic: M1 foundation — domain model and CLI contract core
description:
## Background

omaddons is a single Rust binary whose product is its CLI contract (vision omad-vision-8qa, D2, D17): coding agents drive `omaddons … --json` directly, and the Omarchy widget only renders the same output. Every later M1 area (fsx, state, discovery, sources, the transaction engine, the commands) returns typed outcomes and typed errors, so the vocabulary they share has to exist first:

- the domain types (`Target`, `FolderName`, ids, refs, release sets, addon records);
- the error and warning code registries, with each code's exit code and retryability;
- the JSON envelope, the human renderer and the stderr event stream;
- the clap skeleton: global flags, bare help, usage-error mapping and the panic hook;
- the politeness and safety constants (D22).

The scaffold bead omad-scaffold-fjq (closed, commit 942a1d1) is part of this epic. It created the Cargo package, lints (`unsafe_code` forbidden; clippy `unwrap_used`, `expect_used`, `print_stdout`, `print_stderr`, `dbg_macro` denied), `deny.toml`, the module skeleton, `argc gate` and README v1.

This epic is first in the M1 delivery order ("contract core, fsx, state"). WoW: Forever launches 2026-11-04, and M1 is scoped to land before then.

## Goals

- Domain types in `src/model.rs` that encode safety invariants at the type level: a folder name that cannot escape `AddOns/` and a mutable-folder type that cannot name a `Blizzard_*` folder (D14, D27).
- One closed registry of error codes (code → exit code → retryable) and warning codes in `src/error.rs`. Every error carries a non-empty `fix` plus `fix_argv` (D17, D31).
- The §5.9 envelope: exactly one JSON document on stdout under `--json`, on success and on failure. Human output otherwise, with stdout empty on error. Diagnostics on stderr (NDJSON when stderr is not a TTY).
- A clap skeleton that every command bead extends (DEC-1). Bare `omaddons` prints help and exits 0. Usage errors become `usage` envelopes (exit 2) with a suggested fix. A panic still yields a well-formed `internal` envelope.
- Every §5.13 constant defined exactly once, typed, and listed in a registry that M4's `capabilities.limits` and the config overrides read.

## Success Criteria

When every child is closed:

- `omaddons` (no arguments) prints concise help on stdout and exits 0. `omaddons --json` prints one envelope with `"ok":true,"command":"help"`.
- `omaddons hepl --json` exits 2 and prints one envelope with `error.code == "usage"`, a non-empty `fix` and `fix_argv == ["omaddons","help"]`.
- A panic injected with the debug-only failpoint `cli.panic` under `--json` exits 1 and prints one envelope with `error.code == "internal"` and `fix_argv == ["omaddons","status"]` (DEC-5).
- When stderr is not a TTY, every stderr line parses as JSON and carries an `event` key in `progress|log|warning|error`.
- `ErrorCode` covers every code in vision §5.9 plus the DEC-4 additions (`scope_denied`, `state_too_new`), and a table-driven test checks each code's exit code and retryability.
- `src/politeness.rs` and `src/limits.rs` define every §5.13 constant, and a test checks that the registries list each one, with the config-overridable set matching the vision's "(config)" markings.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Non-Goals

- `capabilities`, `robot-docs`, full intent inference (verb aliases, misplaced target names), `completions` and the wire-name golden test are M4. This epic only provides the registries and serialization they will read.
- The doctor exit dictionary (0–6 plus 64/66/73/74) is M4.
- Real commands (`status`, `install`, …) are E7. Each command bead adds its own subcommand (DEC-1), and there are no stubs.
- Stored plans and `plan_id` are M4.
- `--progress json` events for long operations are emitted by the engine and command beads. This epic defines the event stream and its modes.

## Considerations

- The contract freezes only at M4's first tag, so codes and keys may be added during M1. Each addition is recorded on the vision bead (DEC-4).
- Determinism: under `--json`, struct keys appear in declaration order and map keys are sorted (`BTreeMap`). Data is serialized generically, never round-tripped through `serde_json::Value`: without serde_json's `preserve_order` feature a `Value` object sorts its keys and would break declaration order.
- Data structs derive `Serialize` and `schemars::JsonSchema` from day one (DEC-3).
- Lints deny `print!`/`eprint!`. All output goes through `src/output/` using locked `std::io::Write` handles.
- Children: model, error-registry, constants, output-envelope, cli-skeleton, plus the closed scaffold bead omad-scaffold-fjq.
acceptance_criteria: bare omaddons prints help on stdout and exits 0, and omaddons --json prints one ok:true envelope with command help; omaddons hepl --json exits 2 with error.code usage, a non-empty fix and fix_argv ["omaddons","help"]; the debug failpoint cli.panic under --json exits 1 with one internal envelope whose fix_argv is ["omaddons","status"]; with stderr not a TTY every stderr line is JSON with an event key; ErrorCode covers every vision §5.9 code plus scope_denied and state_too_new, and a table-driven test checks exits and retryability; every §5.13 constant is defined once and listed in its registry; argc gate passes
close_reason: M1 foundation complete: domain model (1.4), error/warning registries (1.3), constants and limit registries (1.2), output envelope and stderr stream (1.5), CLI skeleton (1.1), plus the scaffold

comments.author: BoldKettle
